test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jul 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence.**

Shelley has been **__*contemplating *__**for a few days but still has not decided to quit the job.
solution: The correct answer is: "**chewing the cud**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • "**Chewing the cud**" means to think carefully and slowly about something before making a decision. (निर्णय लेने से पहले किसी चीज़ के बारे में सावधानीपूर्वक और धीरे-धीरे सोचना) • **Example**: *After receiving the job offer, he spent the weekend chewing the cud before deciding to accept it, weighing all the pros and cons carefully.* • This idiom comes from the way cows chew their food, regurgitating it and chewing it again to fully digest it. • In the given sentence, Shelley is taking her time to consider whether or not to quit her job, so "**chewing the cud**" is an **appropriate substitute**. Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** • "**Biting the dust**" is an idiom that refers to being defeated or killed in battle or competition. (युद्ध या प्रतियोगिता में पराजित या मारा जाना) • "**Cooling one's heels**" is an idiom that means to wait for a long time, often in a frustrating or uncomfortable situation. (लंबे समय तक इंतजार करना) • "**Getting into hot waters**" is an idiom that means to get into trouble or face consequences for one's actions. (मुसीबत में पड़ना या अपने कार्यों के परिणाम भुगतना) 150:Ta22, The correct answer is: "**troupe**".
